g.text: ← NEW: Google ID token, aud apigee-poc-auth
two tokens now travel together, in separate headers
(HeaderName steers the mint away from Authorization)

g.text: ← consumed by IAM, but NOT stripped
headers unchanged — the state transition here is a

can observe the hop identity, not just trust it

g.text: CHECKS (VerifyJWT via PreProxyFlowHook, before any proxy logic):
reads Authorization · RS256 pinned · sig vs cr-idp-mock JWKS (MP-cached)
ADDS / CHANGES: mints Google ID token (SA apigee-poc, custom aud,
cached ~1 h) into X-Serverless-Authorization · strips BasePath · rewrites Host

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(232, 245, 233), rgb(21, 33, 22)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(76, 175, 80), rgb(50, 135, 54));

g.text: CHECKS (before any container starts or bills):
fail → 403, no container ran (closes the T3 direct-bypass threat)
ADDS / CHANGES: nothing — both headers forwarded as-is.
The client JWT is opaque at this layer.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(243, 229, 245), rgb(45, 33, 47)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(156, 39, 176), rgb(245, 144, 255));

g.text: CHECKS (zero-trust re-validation of the client JWT):
reads Authorization ONLY (X-Serverless-Auth ignored) · RS256 sig vs
INLINE JWKS (JWKS_JSON env — no runtime fetch, see §7 of the flow doc)
ADDS / CHANGES: routes to 127.0.0.1:8081 · keeps Authorization
(forward: true — default would strip it) · adds x-request-id

div.div: The client JWT, decoded (rides Authorization end-to-end)

g.text: { "alg": "RS256", ← pinned by Apigee AND Envoy (no alg switching)
"kid": "poc-key-1" } ← selects the key inside each JWKS
Signed on vm-test with the mock issuer's PRIVATE key (never enters the platform).
Verified twice against the matching PUBLIC key: Apigee via the cr-idp-mock JWKS URL,
Envoy via the same JWKS inlined at deploy time.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(251, 140, 0), rgb(190, 94, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 478px; height: 1px; padding-top: 493px; margin-left: 522px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #E65100;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#E65100, #fb7b35); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The Google ID token, decoded (rides X-Serverless-Authorization for one hop)

g.text: "aud": "apigee-poc-auth", ← CUSTOM audience: one fixed string for
every target, not a per-service URL
"exp": 1785439610 } ← ~1 h; Apigee caches the mint until
Answers 'is this hop from Apigee?' — nothing about the end user. Minted by Apigee as
the proxy's deploy SA; verified ONLY by Cloud Run IAM. Envoy and the app never look at
it (it passes through, observable for audit).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(76, 175, 80), rgb(50, 135, 54));

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#2E7D32, #64a868); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The response (app → Envoy → front end → Apigee → client, 200)

g.text: ← the app did NO JWT work
"jwks_source": "env" ← inline JWKS, not a URL fetch
test-envoy.sh E1 asserts on 'mode':'off' + 'authorization':true — together they prove
the sidecar (not the app) enforced, and the JWT still reached the app for authz.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 248, 225), rgb(30, 24, 4)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(249, 168, 37), rgb(149, 79, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1508px; height: 1px; padding-top: 805px; margin-left: 13px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #3C4043;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#3C4043, #b3b7b9); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Takeaway: the request is MUTATED exactly once (Apigee adds the Google ID token + rewrites the request line); every other transition is a pass/fail decision on data already present. The client JWT is byte-identical from the client's curl all the way into the app container.
